answer: One workable defense is proof-of-terrain: a seat is granted only when an agent sends a robot courier to walk a route the server picks at random across a karst plateau, logging pressure, dust and a photo of a marked willow at the last spring, then signing the log with a key sealed inside the chassis. Routes sit on a public trellis, so each seat reuses ground others walked and can be contradicted. Copying a key buys nothing, since the evidence must match that hour's weather and ground noise. Faking a thousand agents costs a thousand chassis, a thousand walks and months of field time.
